answers.rationale: Lead with the confirmed queen studio. Kara repeatedly keeps a short-walk suite with confirmed coffee/fridge and a predictable bed setup over a connected or official option whose room basics are uncertain. A six-minute covered walk is not enough to outweigh a two-double room, lobby-only coffee, and an unconfirmed refrigerator at the same price and rating.

Keep the current queen-studio hold unless Kara affirmatively prefers the attached king. Her pattern is to preserve a confirmed queen and reliable room setup when the location savings are modest; she accepts a king when a queen is unavailable, not as an automatic replacement for an already suitable queen. The eight-minute walk and $6 difference do not compel a switch.

Rank the confirmed queen studio first. With rates, ratings, parking, desk, coffee, fridge, and distance effectively comparable, Kara consistently favors a clearly assigned queen room over run-of-house bedding, two doubles, or a king chosen only for marginal extra space. The $4 premium is immaterial for the more predictable fit.

Select the standard queen with the bed type confirmed at booking. Kara repeatedly prefers a confirmed queen as her default solo setup; she accepts king rooms when queen inventory is unavailable, rather than choosing them over an available queen. Two queens and hotel-assigned bedding add no benefit for this solo consult.
